sources.entry: Scoold - Stack Overflow in a JAR. An enterprise-ready Q&A platform with full-text search, SAML, LDAP integration and social login support. (Demo, Source Code) Apache-2.0 Java/Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: Scoold is a self-hostable Q&A and knowledge-sharing platform for teams, inspired by Stack Overflow, packaged as a single Spring Boot JAR and backed by the separate Para server.
summary.what_it_does: Scoold provides Stack Overflow-style questions, answers, voting, and a reputation system with badges for team or organization knowledge sharing. It offers full-text search, suggestions for similar questions, and duplicate-post hints. Teams can be organized into isolated "Spaces," and the platform supports webhooks, a RESTful API defined with OpenAPI 3.0, and Zapier integration. Authentication options in the open-source version include LDAP, mutual TLS, and social login (Facebook, Google, GitHub, LinkedIn, Microsoft, Slack, Amazon, Twitter) with Gravatar. The README says data storage and heavy lifting are delegated to Para, which can use several databases and provides a distributed object cache. Scoold Pro, a paid version, adds features such as SAML, SCIM 2.0, and file uploads to S3 or Azure Blob.
use_cases: company knowledge base for technical questions
notable: Distributed as a single Spring Boot JAR
Delegates data storage to the separate Para backend, which supports multiple databases and multi-tenant 'apps'
Spaces (Teams) give isolated groups of questions and users
caveats: Several enterprise features listed (SAML, SCIM, file uploads, unlimited spaces, multiple admins, anonymous posts) are only in the paid Scoold Pro version
Scoold depends on a separate Para server, so a second service must be deployed and reachable over HTTP(S)
Native image build requires GraalVM to be installed
